text: NOTE 1: As for numIterations parameter in LDPC Decoding, there can be several use cases to apply the optimal number of LDPC decoding iterations, such as- 1\) in a case when more number of LDPC iterations \(as part of the entire allowed processing resources\) should be allocated to URLLC traffic than eMBB traffic if they coexist, 2\) in a case when cell coverage would improve with increased number of LDPC iterations for cell-edge users \(e.g., with minimum MCS and small PDU length\), and 3\) in a case when VoIP such as small data size would be benefited from increased number of LDPC iterations. The numIterations parameter in LDPC Decoding is assumed to be always set by AAL application as same as other parameters in LDPC Decoding, and the support of the numIterations parameter in AALI implementation at HWA is optional \(e.g., the default value is "0", which is set by AAL application when AALI implementation does not support this parameter. In that case, AALI implementation may simply choose to ignore this parameter \(or the value\)\). Note that the aforementioned examples are not meant to be an exhaustive list, and AAL applications may choose to set this parameter for other use cases not mentioned here. The actual range of numIterations parameter value would be as per the AALI implementation.

text: NOTE 2: As for earlyTermination-OnOff parameter in LDPC Decoding, there would be several use cases to optimize the early termination of LDPC decoding iterations, such as – 1\) in a case where it would be preferable to prioritize energy efficiency rather than minimizing the BLER \(which leads to earlyTermination-OnOff to be on\), and 2\) in a case where early termination would be preferable for configured grant. The earlyTermination-OnOff parameter in LDPC Decoding is assumed to be always set by AAL application as same as other parameters in LDPC Decoding, and the support of the earlyTermination-OnOff parameter in AALI implementation at HWA is optional \(e.g., the default value is "0", which means early termination is off. AAL application will ONLY set this value to 1 \(i.e. ON\) when AALI implementation supports this feature.\). Note that the aforementioned examples are not meant to be an exhaustive list, and AAL applications may choose to set this parameter for other use cases not mentioned here.
